stalls.reason: Manufacturers mix connected and non-connected SKUs within one model line with no naming convention that distinguishes them. Could not pin an exact buyable model number. Pivoted to a commercial microwave.
stalls.recommendation: Ranges and refrigerators likely need a different procedure than the rest of kitchen — probably starting from a retailer's filterable spec search rather than from the manufacturer.

surprises: Two things. First, the Chamberlain case broke the ladder rather than fitting it: a vendor can behave appallingly while the hardware in front of you stays perfectly usable offline, and conflating those produces a REJECT that a reader will test and find wrong. Separating tier from vendor_risk made the site strictly more informative. Second, the commercial-grade escape hatch showed up independently in three unrelated domains — laundry (Speed Queen), kitchen (Amana/ACP), and lighting (Intermatic) — which suggests it should be promoted from a SCOUT hint to a first-class discovery strategy: for any consumer category that has gone cloud-first, search the commercial equivalent first rather than last.
